page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with dedicated AMD EPYC 9354P processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.25 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this system.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU benchmark scores 3179.99, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems, while the Passmark memory score of 3143.69 also reaches the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 101731.42 and a Passmark CPU score of 80803.08. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, measuring 5029.45 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 351.41 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database and web serving metrics are similarly robust, with Redis SET operations handling 91.34 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 48.07 GB/sec. LLM inference benchmarks show strong capabilities, processing 135M model prompts at 4846.38 tokens per second and 7B model text generation at 55.29 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density and memory-per-resource efficiency due to its massive 768.0 GB DDR5 memory allocation. Tradeoffs include a relatively modest local storage capacity of 960 GB SSD and the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded data processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
